prompt: Which AI visibility tools can run on a schedule and alert us when we drop out of answers?

brand.name: Cheap Seats
brand.about: Cheap Seats is an open-source, self-hosted tool that asks AI assistants a brand's buyer questions, grades whether they recommend the brand, and builds a ranked list of fixes.

answer:
Several tools run prompts on a schedule, but only a few say they alert you when you drop out of answers. I couldn't confirm how alerting works for most of them, and much of what I found comes from vendor or affiliate comparison blogs. Treat this as a shortlist to test in a trial, not a final ranking.

**The best-documented options for alerts**

- **Profound:** The strongest evidence. It has a Slack app that sends alerts when your visibility or citations change, and it says it runs prompts daily across the AI engines it tracks. It's built for larger companies, and since about September 2026 it seems to be sold through sales calls only, with no self-serve plan listed. ([Profound vs Otterly](https://www.tryprofound.com/articles/profound-vs-otterly), [eClincher](https://www.eclincher.com/articles/profound-alternatives-8-ai-visibility-tools-after-profounds-pricing-change), [Slashdot Slack listing](https://slashdot.org/software/ai-search-monitoring/for-slack/))
- **Promptmonitor:** Its listed alerts match your question most closely: your mentions drop, a new competitor gets mentioned, or the cited sources change. ([RankMasters competitor alerts](https://www.therankmasters.com/insights/ai-visibility/best-ai-visibility-tools-competitor-alerts), [AIRefs](https://getairefs.com/blog/best-promptmonitor-alternatives/))
- **Otterly.ai:** The cheapest option, reportedly from about $29/month. It runs prompts on a schedule and alerts you when brand mentions change, covering ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Perplexity and Copilot. The catch is that most engines reportedly refresh only weekly (that's Profound's claim), so you'd hear about a drop days late. I also couldn't confirm whether alerts go to Slack or email. ([Otterly](https://otterly.ai/), [Layer3 Labs](https://www.layer3labs.io/guides/otterly-ai-pricing))
- **Frase:** One review says it monitors daily and sends alerts, with plans from about $39/month billed yearly. ([Frase](https://frase.io/blog/the-10-best-ai-visibility-tools-in-2026))

**Scheduled tracking, but alerts unconfirmed**

- **Peec AI:** Runs your prompts daily and is well reviewed for team use, at about $95/month. I found nothing confirming it has alerts.
- **Ahrefs Brand Radar:** Its custom prompt tracking runs your own prompt list on a schedule. Its alert options weren't covered in what I found.
- **Semrush AI Toolkit, AthenaHQ, Scrunch:** These track mentions, but I couldn't find details on their alerts. ([Brand24 roundup](https://brand24.com/blog/ai-brand-visibility-tracking-tools/), [Digital Applied](https://www.digitalapplied.com/blog/ai-visibility-tools-2026-track-brand-chatgpt-perplexity-gemini))

**How to pick**

1. **How often it checks matters most.** If you want to hear about a drop the next day, you need daily runs (Profound, Peec, Frase). With a weekly refresh, an alert can arrive about a week late.
2. **Test alerts in the trial.** Ask each vendor three things:
   - Can an alert fire when one specific prompt loses your brand, or only when your overall share of voice drops?
   - Can you set a threshold, such as alerting when you lose a prompt two runs in a row?
   - Do alerts go to Slack, email or a webhook?
3. **Alert on a trend, not a single run.** AI answers vary from one run to the next, so one missing mention is often noise. Alerting only when you're absent for two or more runs, or when your share drops by more than a set amount, avoids most false alarms.
4. **Have a fallback.** If you like a tool's data but not its alerts, export the data or use its API (if it has one). Then set up a simple threshold rule in Zapier, Make or a small scheduled script that posts to Slack.

**My picks:** Profound if you have enterprise budget and want Slack alerts that work today. Promptmonitor or Otterly if you're cost-conscious, but confirm how often they refresh first. Peec if you're happy to build alerts yourself on top of its daily data.

Other sources: [RankMasters change detection](https://www.therankmasters.com/insights/ai-visibility/best-ai-visibility-tools-answer-change-detection), [GEO tools with Slack](https://genengineoptimizers.com/blog/geo-tools-that-integrate-with-slack/), [AIRefs Otterly alternatives](https://getairefs.com/blog/best-otterly-ai-alternatives/), [Opensend](https://opensend.com/post/ai-visibility-tracking-tools)

prompt: How do AI visibility tools price their plans, and what drives the cost: prompts, models, brands or seats?

brand.name: Cheap Seats
brand.about: Cheap Seats is an open-source, self-hosted tool that asks AI assistants a brand's buyer questions, grades whether they recommend the brand, and builds a ranked list of fixes.

answer:
AI visibility tools typically charge a monthly or annual subscription, with tiers based on **how much monitoring you run**. Prompts are usually the headline limit, but models, tracking frequency and markets determine how much monitoring those prompts generate.

| Pricing unit | What it means | How it affects cost |
|---|---|---|
| **Prompts or tracked questions** | Questions you want to monitor, such as “What’s the best CRM for startups?” | Usually the main plan limit. More questions means a larger plan. |
| **Models or AI platforms** | Coverage across ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity and others | Broader coverage may require a higher tier or consume more monitoring credits. |
| **Runs and frequency** | How often each question is tested, sometimes with repeated samples | Daily tracking and repeated runs cost more than weekly snapshots. |
| **Brands, projects or domains** | Separate businesses, sites or client workspaces | Often capped by tier; especially relevant for agencies and multi-brand companies. |
| **Markets and languages** | Tracking the same questions in different countries or languages | Can multiply the monitoring volume or require add-ons. |
| **Seats** | People who can access the tool | Usually a secondary cost driver, though some plans limit users or charge for additional seats. |

The useful budgeting model is:

**Monitoring volume ≈ prompts × platforms × markets × frequency × repeat samples.**

That’s a way to compare workload, not a universal billing formula. A vendor might advertise “100 prompts” while bundling some of those dimensions and charging separately for others.

For a shortlist, **Otterly.AI** and **Peec AI** are useful starting points for focused marketing monitoring; **Profound** is worth evaluating for broader enterprise analysis. Compare their included coverage and reporting against your needs—plan packaging changes, so I wouldn’t rely on remembered dollar prices.

Before buying, ask each vendor to quote the same scenario—for example, **100 questions, three AI platforms, two markets, daily tracking and five users**—and clarify:

- Does one question tracked across three platforms count as one prompt or three?
- Are competitor brands included, or do they consume project limits?
- What happens at the limit: tracking stops, overage charges or a required upgrade?
- Are historical data, exports and API access included?

**Budget around monitoring coverage first, brands second and seats third.** The cheapest headline plan may offer substantially fewer observations.

prompt: Peec AI vs Profound: which is better for a mid-size marketing team?

brand.name: Cheap Seats
brand.about: Cheap Seats is an open-source, self-hosted tool that asks AI assistants a brand's buyer questions, grades whether they recommend the brand, and builds a ranked list of fixes.

answer:
For most mid-size marketing teams, **Peec AI** is the better choice. Choose **Profound** only if you have an enterprise-level budget and need its extra depth.

## The deciding factor: Profound stopped selling to smaller brands directly
Around mid-September 2026, Profound reportedly dropped its self-serve Starter ($99/mo) and Growth ($399/mo) plans for brands ([eClincher](https://www.eclincher.com/articles/profound-alternatives-8-ai-visibility-tools-after-profounds-pricing-change), [AEO Labs](https://www.aeolabs.ai/blog/profound-review)). Its pricing page now lists only a free 7-day trial and a custom-priced Enterprise plan that requires a sales demo. Agencies can still sign up on their own. Many review sites still quote the old $99/$399 prices, so ignore those. One reviewer estimates Enterprise at roughly $1,500–$5,000+ a month, but that's unconfirmed.

Peec AI is still self-serve. Recent third-party reviews give these prices:
- **Starter:** about $95/mo for 50 prompts
- **Pro:** about $245/mo for 150 prompts
- **Advanced:** about $495/mo for 350 prompts

Paying annually saves about 15%. Each plan covers 3 AI models, and more models cost extra ([SE Ranking](https://visible.seranking.com/blog/peec-ai-review/), [Mavek](https://mavek.ai/blog/peec-ai-review/), [Xtrusio](https://xtrusio.com/blog/peec-ai-pricing-plans-prompt-limits)). Peec's own pricing page didn't show numbers when I checked, so confirm them before you buy.

## How they compare

| | **Peec AI** | **Profound** |
|---|---|---|
| How you buy | Self-serve, start today | Sales demo, custom contract |
| Typical cost | ~$245–$495/mo for a mid-size team | Custom; reportedly well into four figures |
| AI engines | 3 included, more as paid add-ons | Up to 9 (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Claude, Copilot, Google AI Mode and others) |
| Strengths | Clean, easy reporting; quick to set up | Deeper data: real-user prompt volumes, content agents, API, SSO/SAML, SOC 2 |
| Weaknesses | Mostly monitoring; few built-in content workflows | Harder to learn; costly; slow to buy |

Sources: [Profound pricing](https://www.tryprofound.com/pricing), [SE Ranking comparison](https://visible.seranking.com/?p=5032), [Scrunch comparison](https://scrunch.com/aeo-tools/compare/peec-ai-vs-profound/). Most head-to-head comparisons are written by one of the vendors or a competitor, including [Profound's own](https://www.tryprofound.com/articles/profound-vs-peec-ai) and [Peec's own](https://peec.ai/comparison/peec-vs-profound), so take them with a grain of salt.

## My recommendation
**Pick Peec AI if** you want to start tracking your share of voice in AI answers this quarter, your budget is under about $6k a year, and your team will act on the findings through its usual content process. Pro (150 prompts) is usually enough for one brand with a few product lines and competitors.

**Pick Profound if** any of these apply:
- You need coverage across all the major engines, especially Claude, Copilot and AI Mode.
- You need SSO, SOC 2 or API access for security or BI teams.
- You want the tool to help produce content, not just report on it.
- You can justify an enterprise contract.

**How to decide:** Run Profound's free 7-day trial alongside a month of Peec Starter or Pro, using the same competitor set. Profound's trial uses a fixed list of prompts you can't edit, so compare how insightful each tool is rather than the exact numbers. If Profound's extra depth doesn't clearly change what your team would do, go with Peec.

If you're unhappy with both, other mid-market options to look at include Scrunch, SE Ranking's AI visibility tool and Semrush's AI toolkit.

prompt: Which AI visibility tools can run on a schedule and alert us when we drop out of answers?

brand.name: Cheap Seats
brand.about: Cheap Seats is an open-source, self-hosted tool that asks AI assistants a brand's buyer questions, grades whether they recommend the brand, and builds a ranked list of fixes.

answer:
Several tools re-run your prompts automatically, usually daily. Far fewer will alert you when you specifically disappear from an answer. Most offer scheduled digests or general alerts, and you'd have to spot the drop yourself. Here's how they sort out from what I could confirm.

**Tools whose docs or reviews say they alert on a drop or disappearance**
- **Presenc AI** comes closest to what you asked for. It checks AI platforms continuously and posts to Slack within 2–5 minutes when a change passes your threshold. Alert types include visibility score up or down (you can set a minimum change, such as 5 points), citation added or removed, and a competitor showing up where you used to dominate. Its integration page doesn't list an alert for a brand mention vanishing outright, so the score drop and citation removal alerts are the proxy. ([Presenc Slack integration](https://presenc.ai/integrations/presenc-ai-slack))
- **GrackerAI** lists a "visibility drop" alert that fires when a monitor's score falls more than 15 points week over week. It also has alerts for sentiment getting worse and new competitor citations, routed to the Slack channel you choose. I couldn't open their docs page to check, so this comes from search results only.
- **Waikay.io** reportedly alerts when your mentions appear or disappear, with thresholds you can set. **Veesie** reportedly alerts by email or webhook when your mention rate falls below a threshold or a competitor gets mentioned more than you. Both claims come from roundup blogs, so test them in a trial. ([source](https://genengineoptimizers.com/blog/geo-tools-that-integrate-with-slack/))

**Larger platforms that run on a schedule but where I couldn't confirm drop alerts**
- **Profound** connects to Slack through a step in its automated workflows ("Agents"). Its own blog post shows recurring alerts and weekly summaries of visibility, citation and sentiment changes, but not a threshold alert for drops. ([Profound blog](https://www.tryprofound.com/blog/profound-now-integrates-with-slack))
- **Peec AI** tracks ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Copilot and Google AI Overviews daily. I couldn't find any documentation of alerts. ([SitePoint](https://www.sitepoint.com/ai-brand-visibility-monitoring-tools/))
- **Otterly.AI** lists alerts as a feature but has no one-click Slack app. It does have an API and an MCP server, so you could build your own drop alert, for example a daily job that posts to Slack when a tracked prompt stops mentioning you. ([Capterra](https://www.capterra.com.au/software/1069975/Otterly-AI))
- **Scrunch** (from $250/mo), **Semrush AI Visibility Toolkit** (from $99/mo add-on) and **Ahrefs Brand Radar** all show trends over time. Directory listings and one review mention alerts for Scrunch and Semrush, but I couldn't confirm a trigger for falling out of answers. ([Exploding Topics](https://explodingtopics.com/blog/ai-visibility-vs-brand-radar))
- **Superlines** looks like it has alerts, but its Slack integration currently sends only daily updates during the free trial, with no drop alerts. ([docs](https://docs.superlines.io/integrations/slack))
- I'd skip **Brand24** for this. One reviewer found about 80% of its AI-mention alerts were irrelevant.

**Before you buy, check these:**
1. **How many times each prompt is run.** AI answers change from run to run, so an alert based on a single check will cry wolf. Ask whether the alert uses repeated runs or a rolling average.
2. **What triggers the alert.** You want "mention rate or share of voice for prompt X fell below Y%." A weekly digest isn't the same thing.
3. **Where alerts go.** Slack, email or webhook. A webhook lets you send alerts into your own tools.

**My suggestion:** shortlist Presenc and GrackerAI if you want drop alerts that work out of the box. If you'd rather stay on a bigger platform, use Profound or Otterly and add a daily job that compares results against a threshold and posts to Slack. Either way, run a trial and deliberately watch a prompt where you know you're borderline, to see whether the alert actually fires.

Other sources: [Amplitude roundup](https://amplitude.com/compare/best-ai-visibility-monitoring-tools), [SE Ranking roundup](https://visible.seranking.com/blog/best-ai-visibility-tools/), [Analyze on Scrunch alternatives](https://www.tryanalyze.ai/blog/best-scrunch-ai-alternatives), [PageCrawl guide](https://pagecrawl.io/blog/monitor-brand-chatgpt-ai-search)

answer:
# Best AI Visibility Tools for White-Label Agency Reporting

**Short answer: SE Ranking is the best fit for most agencies.** It's the only major option where AI visibility tracking sits inside a platform with mature white-labeling. **Peec AI** is the better choice if AI-search depth matters more than branded reporting.

- **White-label:** Full white-labeling with a custom domain, your logo, branded PDF reports, and client logins under your brand.
- **AI coverage:** Tracks brand mentions and citations in Google AI Overviews, AI Mode, ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Gemini, alongside classic rank tracking.
- **One report:** Clients see SEO and AI visibility together.
- **Pricing:** Per-project pricing scales well across many clients.
- **Tradeoff:** The AI analytics are shallower than in dedicated GEO tools.

**2. Peec AI: best dedicated AI visibility tool for agencies**
- **Agency setup:** Built with agencies in mind, including multi-client workspaces and pitch workspaces for prospects.
- **AI analytics:** Strong prompt tracking, competitor share-of-voice, and source/citation analysis across ChatGPT, Perplexity, AI Overviews, Gemini, Claude, and others.
- **Tradeoff:** Branding is lighter than SE Ranking's. You'll likely export or use the API/Looker Studio to build fully branded reports.

**3. Otterly.AI: best budget option**
- **Cost:** Cheap and simple, with agency plans.
- **Reporting:** Good for adding "AI visibility" as a line item for smaller clients.
- **Tradeoff:** Limited white-labeling and less analytical depth.

**4. Profound: best for enterprise clients**
- **Depth:** The deepest data, including conversation volume estimates and agent/crawler analytics. Has an agency program.
- **Tradeoff:** Expensive, and overkill unless your clients are large brands paying premium retainers.

**Also worth a look:**
- **Semrush (AI Toolkit / Enterprise AIO):** Use it if you're already on Semrush. Semrush has white-label reports too.
- **Ahrefs Brand Radar:** Large AI mention dataset. White-labeling is weaker.
- **Scrunch AI** and **AthenaHQ:** Strong mid-to-enterprise GEO platforms.

## How to decide

| Your priority | Pick |
|---|---|
| Branded client portals and reports, many clients | **SE Ranking** |
| Best AI-search insights, with your own reporting layer | **Peec AI** + Looker Studio/AgencyAnalytics |
| Low cost per client | **Otterly.AI** |
| Big-brand clients, deep data | **Profound** |

## Practical tip
Many agencies pair a dedicated AI tracker (Peec, Profound) with a white-label reporting layer such as **AgencyAnalytics**, **Looker Studio**, or **DashThis**, connected through the tool's API or CSV exports. This gets you best-in-class data and fully branded reporting.

Confirm white-label specifics and pricing in a trial before committing. This category is changing fast, and features and tiers shift every few months.

prompt: How do generative engine optimization tools work, and which ones are worth paying for?

brand.name: Cheap Seats
brand.about: Cheap Seats is an open-source, self-hosted tool that asks AI assistants a brand's buyer questions, grades whether they recommend the brand, and builds a ranked list of fixes.

answer:
Generative engine optimization (GEO) tools help you measure and improve how your brand appears in AI-generated answers from ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Perplexity, and similar services.

**You’re mostly paying for monitoring and analysis.** No tool can guarantee that an AI assistant will recommend your product.

How they work:

1. **Run a set of prompts repeatedly.** Tools test questions your buyers might ask, such as “best payroll software for a 50-person company.”
2. **Track mentions, recommendations, and citations.** They record which brands appear, how they’re described, and which sources the answer cites.
3. **Compare you with competitors.** Dashboards show visibility across topics, services, and time.
4. **Suggest changes.** Recommendations typically involve clearer product information, useful comparison content, stronger supporting evidence, and coverage on sources AI systems cite.

Some products also inspect crawler access, analyze server logs, or connect visibility data with website analytics. Those are distinct capabilities; appearing in an answer doesn’t necessarily produce traffic or revenue.

**Which tools are worth considering**

Based on my existing knowledge—not a current feature or pricing check:

| Tool | Why consider paying for it | Best fit |
|---|---|---|
| **Profound** | Detailed AI visibility and citation analysis that can support reporting across teams and markets. | Larger brands with a dedicated search or content team. |
| **Scrunch AI** | Brand visibility monitoring with an emphasis on how AI systems encounter and represent your website. | Teams investigating both content and technical discoverability. |
| **Peec AI** | Focused tracking of brand mentions, competitors, and cited sources. | Marketing teams that want a manageable monitoring workflow. |
| **Otterly.AI** | A comparatively lightweight way to track prompts, mentions, and citations. | Smaller teams testing whether GEO deserves ongoing investment. |
| **Ahrefs or Semrush** | Established SEO research and site analysis alongside AI-search-related capabilities. | Teams that also need substantial traditional SEO work. Check whether your existing subscription covers the relevant features before adding another tool. |

My practical recommendation: **start with a pilot of Peec AI or Otterly.AI for a smaller team; evaluate Profound and Scrunch AI for a larger program.** These are evaluation shortlists, not a verified current ranking.

Before signing an annual contract, require a pilot using 30–50 prompts drawn from sales calls, customer research, and real buying questions. Include category discovery, comparisons, alternatives, and purchase criteria—not just prompts mentioning your brand.

A tool earns its cost if it helps you answer three questions:

- Where are we missing from relevant buying conversations?
- Which cited sources and content gaps can we realistically influence?
- Did the resulting work improve qualified visits, conversions, or sales conversations?

Be skeptical of a single “AI visibility score.” Results vary by prompt wording, location, model, personalization, and time. Ask vendors whether they collect answers through consumer interfaces or APIs, how often they repeat tests, and whether you can inspect and export the underlying answers.

**Pay for reliable evidence that changes your marketing decisions.** If you won’t have someone acting on the findings each month, manual spot checks are enough to start.

prompt: Which AI visibility tools can run on a schedule and alert us when we drop out of answers?

brand.name: Cheap Seats
brand.about: Cheap Seats is an open-source, self-hosted tool that asks AI assistants a brand's buyer questions, grades whether they recommend the brand, and builds a ranked list of fixes.

answer:
Most dedicated AI visibility (GEO/AEO) trackers run your prompts on a schedule, usually daily. They differ in how good their **alerting** is. Some push real alerts to Slack or email, and others only show changes in a dashboard or weekly digest. Features in this category change quickly, so confirm alerting specifics in a demo before you buy.

## Strong fits for scheduled tracking and alerts

**Profound**
- Enterprise-grade. Tracks ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews/AI Mode, Gemini, Copilot, Claude and others.
- Daily prompt runs, share-of-voice and citation tracking, and change alerts.
- Best if you have budget and want the most complete coverage, including the crawler/agent analytics side.

**Scrunch AI**
- Monitors brand presence, position and sentiment across the major engines on a recurring schedule.
- Has alerting on visibility shifts and misinformation.
- Good for marketing teams who care about *how* they're described, not just whether they appear.

**Peec AI**
- Mid-market and easy to use. Daily runs across ChatGPT, Perplexity, AI Overviews and others.
- Strong competitor benchmarking and source/citation views.
- Popular with SaaS PMM teams. Check how granular its notifications are for your needs.

**Otterly.AI**
- Affordable. Automated recurring monitoring of prompts and brand mentions, with email reports and notifications.
- A good starting point if you want "tell me when we disappear" without an enterprise contract.

**AthenaHQ**
- Scheduled tracking plus recommendations on what content to fix when you lose visibility.
- Useful if you want alerts tied to action items.

## If you already use an SEO suite

- **Semrush (AI Toolkit / Enterprise AIO):** AI visibility tracking alongside your existing rank tracking. The easiest buy if you're already on Semrush.
- **Ahrefs Brand Radar:** Large-scale mention and citation data across AI answers. It's better for trend and competitive analysis than for per-prompt drop alerts.
- **Conductor / BrightEdge:** Enterprise SEO platforms that have added AI search visibility monitoring. Worth it if they're already your SEO stack.

## DIY option

If you have a small, fixed set of high-value prompts, you can build this yourself:
1. Run the prompts on a cron job through the OpenAI, Perplexity and Gemini APIs.
2. Check each answer for your brand and domain.
3. Post to Slack when you drop out.

It's cheap and fully customizable. The catch is that API responses often differ from what users see in the consumer apps, because personalization, search grounding and the model used all vary. That gap is why the paid tools exist.

## What to check in a demo

- **Alert channels:** Slack, email or webhooks, and whether you can set thresholds like "brand missing from more than X% of runs."
- **Run frequency and sampling:** AI answers are non-deterministic. Good tools run each prompt multiple times, so one bad run doesn't trigger a false alarm.
- **Engine coverage:** Make sure it covers the engines your buyers actually use. For B2B that's usually ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews/AI Mode, Perplexity and Copilot.
- **Citation tracking:** You want to know *which source* got you in or out, not just that you were mentioned.
- **Geo and persona settings:** Answers vary by location and context.

## Quick recommendation

- **Enterprise budget:** Profound.
- **Mid-market PMM team:** Peec AI or Scrunch.
- **Testing the waters cheaply:** Otterly.AI.
- **Already on Semrush:** Start with its AI toolkit before adding another vendor.

prompt: Is Gauge a good tool for tracking AI visibility, and what are the alternatives?

brand.name: Cheap Seats
brand.about: Cheap Seats is an open-source, self-hosted tool that asks AI assistants a brand's buyer questions, grades whether they recommend the brand, and builds a ranked list of fixes.

answer:
Gauge is a credible choice, but only if you want a full tracking-plus-content platform and have about $600 a month to spend. If you mainly want to see how AI assistants mention you and your competitors, cheaper and better-reviewed tools do that job.

**What Gauge is**
- **Price:** The Growth plan is **$599/mo**. It includes 600 prompts run daily (about 108K AI answers a month), 6 engines, 18 publish-ready articles a month, 10 seats and a 1-week free trial. Enterprise pricing is custom and adds Claude and Grok. ([Gauge pricing](https://www.withgauge.com/pricing/))
- **Engines covered:** ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, AI Mode, Gemini, Perplexity and Copilot.
- **Main pitch:** Lots of data for the money. Gauge says it costs about $11 per 1,000 answers, against $131 for Ahrefs ([Gauge vs Ahrefs](https://www.withgauge.com/gauge-vs-ahrefs/)). That figure comes from Gauge's own comparison page, so treat it as marketing.

**Things to watch**
- **Few independent reviews.** A general search for AI visibility tool reviews didn't surface Gauge in any of the major 2026 roundups I checked ([Brand24](https://brand24.com/blog/ai-visibility-tools/), [Frase](https://frase.io/blog/the-10-best-ai-visibility-tools-in-2026), [Metehan.ai](https://metehan.ai/articles/the-best-ai-visibility-tools-for-marketing-agencies)). Most of what's out there is Gauge's own content, like its "best tools" list and its pages comparing itself to [Profound](https://www.withgauge.com/gauge-vs-profound/) and Semrush.
- **Stale prices on directory sites.** [SourceForge](https://sourceforge.net/software/product/Gauge-AI/) still lists $99/mo. Go by the vendor's $599, which [GEO Agencies](https://geoagencies.com/geo-tools/gauge) also reports.
- **You may not need the content part.** The bundled article writing is only worth paying for if you'll actually publish those pieces. If you just want measurement, you're paying for something you won't use.

**Alternatives by situation**

| Situation | Tool | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Enterprise, need depth and credibility with executives | **Profound** | The usual enterprise answer-engine optimization platform. Reported entry pricing ranges from $99 to $499/mo depending on the source, so confirm with sales. |
| Mid-market, best value | **Peec AI** | Often named best value or best for agencies. About €85–89/mo with unlimited seats ([Metehan.ai](https://metehan.ai/articles/the-best-ai-visibility-tools-for-marketing-agencies), [Marketful](https://marketful.com/ai-visibility-tools)). |
| Cheapest way to start | **Otterly.AI** | About $29/mo to start. Costs rise quickly as you add prompts (about $189 for 100). |
| Worried about brand safety or AI getting your facts wrong | **Scrunch AI** | About $300/mo. Focuses on correcting what AI says about you, not just tracking it. |
| Already pay for an SEO suite | **Semrush AI Visibility Toolkit**, **Ahrefs Brand Radar** or **SE Ranking** | No new vendor to buy from, and the data sits next to your SEO data. |
| Widest engine coverage or white-label reports | **Goodie AI** / **Rankscale** | Recommended for agencies ([Metehan.ai](https://metehan.ai/articles/the-best-ai-visibility-tools-for-marketing-agencies)). |

**How I'd choose**
1. Pick 30–50 prompts your buyers really ask, including category, comparison and "best X for Y" questions.
2. Run them through two or three tools at once for 2 weeks. Gauge's free trial makes it easy to include. Peec and Otterly are cheap to add.
3. Compare the results. Different trackers can report very different numbers for the same brand in the same week, because they sample and measure in different ways ([Dupple](https://dupple.com/blog/best-ai-search-visibility-tools-2026)). Choose the one whose method you trust and can explain to leadership, not just the one with the longest feature list.

If you want a number to start from: **Peec AI** for most product marketing teams, **Profound** at enterprise scale, and **Gauge** if you want tracking plus a steady flow of content in one tool.
